newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil prices mostly steady, cargoes soften.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil prices mostly steady, cargoes soften.

text.p: NWE fuel oil prices were mostly steady on Monday, but trade was thin.
Traders said high sulphur barges had made early gains of $2 a tonne on the back of some light short-covering stemming Friday's sharp sell-off, but later trade was very thin.
High sulphur barges traded at $111, $112 and $112.50 for running refinery material fob Rotterdam and were valued around $112.50 in late business.
Esso Netherlands confirmed on Monday its Rotterdam refinery was running as normal after the small "hiccup" at its flexi-coker unit on Friday.
News of problems with coker which consumes the equivalent of about 7,000 tonnes of heavy fuel a day triggered Friday's sell off, traders said.

Stable crude initially encouraged sellers to peg cargo prices a little higher, but there was little sign of fresh trader or utility buying today and this combined with sharp later crude losses saw prices looking soft around $112.50 a tonne cif NWE.
Low sulphur fuel oil trade remained quiet with Barges holding around $120/123 fob ARA and cargoes at $115/117 a tonne fob NWE.
